title: US vaccination rates fall again as exemptions continue to rise, CDC data shows
gist: New CDC data show US kindergarten vaccination rates fell again in 2025-2026 (MMR to 92.4 percent) while nonmedical exemptions jumped to 4 percent, with 24 states now above the 5 percent exemption threshold as the US nears losing measles-elimination status amid RFK Jr.-led federal anti-vaccine policy.

insights.claim: National kindergarten MMR vaccination fell to 92.4 percent and DTaP to 92.0 percent in 2025-2026, below the 95 percent herd-immunity threshold, with only 10 states at or above 95 percent for MMR.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Falling coverage raises outbreak risk with public-health and healthcare-cost implications; a macro-social risk indicator.

insights.claim: Nonmedical exemptions rose to 4 percent (from 3.2 percent), and 24 states now have exemption rates at or above the 5 percent level that precludes reaching 95 percent coverage—up from 14 states in 2023-2024.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Accelerating exemption growth signals a structural, policy-driven decline in coverage rather than a temporary dip.
insights.locator: the number of children with exemptions

insights.claim: Under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the CDC released the data without its usual full MMWR analysis, and Trump and Kennedy announced an executive order to reduce recommended vaccinations as US measles cases hit a 34-year high.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Federal policy is actively undermining vaccination norms—material for healthcare, pharma, and public-health exposure.
